text: Course six's capstone built a scoped application tracking equipment loaned out to employees, with an equipment table and a request table that extends task. The ask now: an external facilities dashboard needs to look up a single checkout request's status over REST, without logging into the instance. This lab exposes that one request as a versioned Scripted REST API.

The API definition is named Equipment Checkout API, base path /api/x_acme_eqchk, with a required role so only the equipment admin role or an admin can call anything under it at all — checked before any script runs. A Version record named v1 contributes the /v1 segment. The Resource's relative path is /checkout/ followed by the sys_id, method GET.

The script pulls the sys_id straight out of the path, then runs the familiar one-line GlideRecord lookup. When that lookup finds nothing, it returns false — exactly the signal the script uses to set status 404 and return early, before ever building a response body from fields that don't exist.

An optional query parameter lets the caller ask for the full approval history. Since every query parameter arrives as a string, comparing it to the literal string true is what actually turns it into a real boolean. The response dot-walks through the equipment reference field to read the equipment's own name, and only adds the approved-by field when history was explicitly requested.

A real call with include_history=true returns the checkout's number, status, requester, equipment name, and dates, plus who approved it. Leave that parameter off, and the response is smaller by exactly that one field. A 404 call gets a clean error body instead, with nothing else in it, so the dashboard can branch cleanly on the status code alone.

v1 answers one question: what's this checkout's current status. A v2 could add a computed overdue flag or a list-everything resource, each as its own new Resource under its own new Version — neither touches v1's script, so the dashboard calling v1 today keeps working exactly as built, even after v2 ships.
